subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class per-skill user preference sidecar, and if so should the public contract be Markdown sidecar, structured skill config, or no core support?
rationale: The feature is absent in current and shipped source, but adding it changes public skill loading, prompt composition, snapshot invalidation, sandbox/read boundaries, and documentation rather than fixing an already-defined bug.

options.title: Standardize Markdown sidecar
options.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that loads at lower precedence with the selected skill and participates in prompt-version, watcher, sandbox, and docs behavior.

options.title: Use structured skill config
options.body: Keep preferences under `skills.entries.*.config` and require skills or plugins to interpret them, avoiding a new prompt-side Markdown surface but weakening natural-language convention support.

options.title: Decline core support
options.body: Keep the current model of full skill overrides, Skill Workshop proposals, global memory/context, or manual skill instructions if maintainers do not want another skill-loading surface.

recommendation.title: Standardize Markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Add a documented `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` sidecar that loads at lower precedence with the selected skill and participates in prompt-version, watcher, sandbox, and docs behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily product/API direction, and this account has relevant skill docs/product history plus timeline routing on this issue.
